industry: Nuclear Components and Services / Aerospace and Defense
thesis: BWXT is the sole-source manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for the U.S. Navy and the largest Western supplier of commercial nuclear components, giving it a regulatory-moated, multi-decade revenue base. FY2026 guidance was raised twice to ~$3.80B revenue, $662M-$672M adjusted EBITDA and $4.70-$4.80 non-GAAP EPS, with backlog at a record $8.40B (+40% YoY) and Commercial Operations revenue up 72% in Q2. The stock nonetheless set a 52-week low of $133.90 on 28 Sep 2026, down 26% over one year and 44% from its $241.82 high, as the entire nuclear/AI-power complex de-rated. The mismatch between accelerating fundamentals and a collapsing multiple is the opportunity; the risk is that ~28x forward earnings still leaves room for further compression.

drivers: Backlog converts as guided: record $8.40B total backlog (+40% YoY), Government Operations alone $6.80B
Commercial Operations compounds at 40%+ — Q2 2026 revenue +72% YoY with segment adjusted EBITDA up 123%
Janus microreactor program scales from phased Fort Campbell award into a repeatable installed-base business
Up to $800M of Nordic Capital medical proceeds redeployed into commercial nuclear capacity or buybacks
Multiple re-rates back toward early-2026 levels (~30x EV/FY2026E adjusted EBITDA) as the nuclear de-rating exhausts

base_case.assumptions: FY2026 lands inside guidance (~$3.80B revenue, $4.70-$4.80 non-GAAP EPS, $345M-$360M FCF) and FY2027 non-GAAP EPS reaches the ~$5.26 consensus. Government Operations grows high single digits on naval propulsion and special materials; Commercial Operations grows 25-35% with PCG contributing a full year. The stock re-rates to 29-35x FY2027E EPS, roughly a 25-30% discount to the $213.75 sell-side consensus target.

risks: Nuclear/AI-power theme keeps unwinding and BWXT is valued like a conventional defense prime at ~20-23x earnings
Government Operations margin erosion persists — Q2 2026 segment operating income fell 3% YoY on mix and fewer favorable contract adjustments
Federal budget disruption: continuing resolutions, shutdowns or appropriations delays push naval propulsion and NNSA bookings right
Bookings lumpiness bites: Q2 2026 bookings of $649M versus $1,640M a year earlier
Growth capex and $2.02B of long-term debt (debt/equity 1.51) compress free cash flow if commercial nuclear orders slow

catalysts.event: FY2027 U.S. defense appropriations and naval propulsion / NNSA award flow — the main driver of Government Operations bookings
Q3 print: test of the raised FY2026 guidance (~$3.80B revenue, $4.70-$4.80 non-GAAP EPS) and first full quarter of PCG
Close of the up-to-$800M medical divestiture to Nordic Capital, including capital-allocation decision on proceeds
FY2026 results and initiation of FY2027 guidance — first clean look at the post-medical, PCG-inclusive earnings base
Janus Phase 1 milestones: Fort Campbell site selection, Army/NRC regulatory process start and TRISO fuel fabrication ramp

key_risks: Revenue concentration: roughly 70% of revenue comes from U.S. government customers, dominated by the Navy's nuclear propulsion program and NNSA
Still-premium valuation — ~28x FY2026E non-GAAP EPS and ~21x EV/FY2026E adjusted EBITDA despite the 44% drawdown
Government Operations margins are flat-to-down as favorable contract adjustments normalize
Balance sheet leverage: $2.02B long-term debt against $1.33B equity (debt/equity 1.51)
Advanced-reactor revenue is phased and small today; microreactor revenue actually declined in 2025
Heavy growth capex (FY2025 $184.6M, H1 2026 $83.9M) constrains near-term free cash flow conversion
Divesting the medical business removes a fast-growing, higher-margin unit and creates redeployment risk
Momentum and flows are hostile: below the 50-day ($159.46) and 200-day ($190.54) averages, and removed from several Russell 1000 Defensive-style indexes in June 2026
